nomad_overview.ov_status_detached: DETACHED. The Flotilla is detached.%s It consumes from its own stores (including the monthly supply of its ships) until it rejoins.

nomad_flotilla.card_mothballed_tip: The %s is mothballed. It takes up Space, needs no staff, and does nothing.

nomad_flotilla.cards_tip_remote: With Remote mining on, the Mining Rig mines anywhere inside a star system that has fully surveyed deposits or asteroids, at a much lower rate. It takes %s days to turn on, and turns off immediately.
nomad_flotilla.cards_tip_scrap: Scrap this Work. This happens immediately.
nomad_flotilla.cards_tip_priority: Residents staff High priority Works first, then Medium, then Low. Changing a Work's priority is free and takes effect at the next economy tick.
nomad_flotilla.hover_unknown_work: The mod that added this Work is not installed, so its sizes are unknown.
nomad_flotilla.hover_group_makes: Makes each month at 100% global efficiency
nomad_flotilla.hover_group_uses: Consumes each month at 100% global efficiency
nomad_flotilla.hover_mining_note: Mining rates are for each resource the body has, at a 1.0x deposit.
nomad_flotilla.hover_brokerage_note: Above 100% global efficiency, credits only receive %s of the increase. Units sold get all of the increase.
nomad_flotilla.hover_brokerage_now: At %s global efficiency: %s x %s = %s a month, and it sells up to %s units.
nomad_flotilla.hover_brokerage_now_yield: At %s global efficiency: %s x %s x %s yield = %s a month, and it sells up to %s units.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_hydroponic_farm: Grows Food. It needs no inputs.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_supplies_factory: Makes Supplies from Metals and Transplutonics.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_luxury_goods_factory: Makes Luxury Goods from Domestic Goods.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_refinery: Refines Ore into Metals and Transplutonic Ore into Transplutonics. If one ore runs out, the other is still refined.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_machinery_factory: Makes Heavy Machinery from Metals and Transplutonics.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_mining_rig: The Flotilla mines while within range of a fully surveyed body. The speed is based on the deposit. Having multiple resource types does not decrease the individual rate.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_foundry: Runs the autoforge, which builds ships, weapons and fighter wings. It turns Metals, Transplutonics, and Heavy Machinery into Foundry production while a job is queued.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_brokerage: Your Flotilla runs a financial business. The Brokerage takes a fee, giving you credits each month. It also lets you sell the commodities you marked Sell or Sell cargo, the most expensive first.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_military_fabricator: Makes Heavy Armaments from Metals and Transplutonics.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_organ_harvester: Consumes residents to make Harvested Organs. It is idle while consuming more residents would lower the Basic Needs level.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_marine_barracks: Trains residents as marines and arms them with Heavy Armaments. The marines join your fleet, up to a target you set.
nomad_flotilla.hover_harvester_embryo: The Biofactory Embryo is installed, so it consumes no residents.
nomad_flotilla.hover_gate_freight_office_done: The Flotilla went through a Gate this month.
nomad_flotilla.hover_gate_freight_office_none: The Flotilla has not gone through a Gate this month.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_survey_office: Reduces the supplies and heavy machinery required to survey planets.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_stealth_control_room: Reduces the range at which the fleet can be detected.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_slipstream_chart_room: Reveals the slipstreams near the fleet.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_repair_yard: Every ship in the fleet recovers combat readiness and repairs faster.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_raid_training_ground: Residents drill with your marines. The fleet's ground raids are stronger, and marines gain experience over time.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_family_cabins: Houses the crews' families. Increases the maximum combat readiness of crewed Nomad ships.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_guild_hall: Residents organize their trades here. Increases global efficiency.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_damage_control_room: Nomad ships repair disabled weapons and engines faster in combat.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_gunnery_range: Point-defense weapons on Nomad ships have more range and deal more damage.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_officer_academy: Increases the number of officers you can command.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_hospital: Treats crew wounded in battle. Some of the crew the fleet loses return as residents.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_watch_stations: Residents stand extra watches. Increases the peak operating time of Nomad ships.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_tinkering_facilities: Tunes Nomad ships for a higher turn rate, top speed, flux dissipation and flux capacity.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_storm_shielding_workshop: Fits Nomad ships with storm shielding. Hyperspace storms and star coronas affect them less.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_passenger_terminal: While the Flotilla orbits one of your colonies, the colony gains stability and migrants join.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_purchasing_office: You get a rebate on your market purchases.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_tug_bay: Increases the fleet's maximum burn level.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_restoration_bay: You can repair d-mods away from a market, at the same cost in Domain-grade Parts. The Restoration Bay has no effect if you have the Hull Restoration skill.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_domain_parts_workshop: The Foundry can build Domain-grade Parts while the Domain Parts Workshop is running.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_lobster_farm: Raises Volturnian lobster in seawater pens. Makes Luxury Goods from Food.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_gate_freight_office: Carries freight through the Gates. You are paid each month the Flotilla goes through one.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_school: The population grows faster while Basic Needs is Normal or better.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_patrol_supply_depot: Sells provisions to the patrols of the faction that commissioned you. You are paid each month.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_cargo_shuttle_bay: While the Flotilla orbits one of your colonies, the colony gains accessibility.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_insurance_office: When a Nomad ship is lost in battle, you are paid a share of its hull's base value. Nothing is paid for a ship you recover, or for a ship lost while the Flotilla is detached.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_insurance_office_survival: When a Nomad ship is lost in battle, you are paid a share of its hull's base value before Survival Mode's multiplier. The codex shows the value after it. Nothing is paid for a ship you recover, or for a ship lost while the Flotilla is detached.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_assault_course: Marines trained at the Marine Barracks join your fleet with some experience.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_welding_shop: Nomad ships need fewer supplies to recover and repair. Each ship saves at least 1 supply.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_shops: Sells everyday goods to residents. Lowers the Basic Needs requirement.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_theater: Residents put on shows here. Lowers the Basic Needs requirement.
nomad_flotilla.hover_desc_luxury_quarters: Large private cabins for residents. Lowers the Basic Needs requirement.
nomad_flotilla.hover_support_rule: Support Works only have an effect while Basic Needs is Spartan or better.
nomad_flotilla.hover_idle_input: The Work makes nothing until %s is back in stock.
nomad_flotilla.hover_idle_output: The Work makes nothing until the store has room for more %s.
nomad_flotilla.hover_idle_input_detached: The Work makes nothing until %s is back in stock. A detached Flotilla consumes only from its own stores.
nomad_flotilla.hover_idle_output_detached: The store has no room for more %s.

nomad_flotilla.marines_idle_detached: New marines join your fleet, so none are trained while the Flotilla is detached.

nomad_flotilla.marines_idle_no_room: Your fleet has no room for more crew or marines.

nomad_flotilla.marines_target_field_tip: Type a whole number of marines.
nomad_flotilla.fixui_suspended_tip: Works are suspended, lowest priority first, when they do not fit the Flotilla's Space. A suspended Work uses no Space and no staff.
nomad_flotilla.fixui_suspended_returning: It fits again, and resumes at the next economy tick.
nomad_flotilla.fixui_suspended_no_space: It requires %s Space, and %s is free. It resumes once it fits. Add ships, lower a target or scrap a Work.

nomad_manual.man_intro_1: The Flotilla is a population of migrants living aboard your ships. The Flotilla's population and stores are separate from your own cargo and crew.
nomad_manual.man_basics_1: The Flotilla has {{Berths}} and {{Space}}. {{Berths}} are where the population lives, and they limit how many residents can live in the Flotilla. {{Space}} is used for either (1) storing resource commodities, (2) building {{Works}}, which either produce resources or buff your Flotilla in various ways, or (3) {{Basic Needs}}, which automatically uses the rest.
nomad_manual.man_basics_2: You add a ship to the Flotilla by adding a Nomad hullmod to it, which converts a percentage of its quarters to {{Berths}} and of its cargo capacity to {{Space}}. Both percentages default to {dedication_default} (also the minimum). To change them, press the + button beside the hullmod on the refit screen while docked at a spaceport or station.
nomad_manual.man_works_1: Everything the Flotilla does comes from a {{Work}}. You build Works on the Overview tab with {{Add Work}}, and you can have one of each. Production Works make resources, Foundry production or credits. All other Works are support Works, which buff your fleet or your Flotilla.
nomad_manual.man_works_2: Each size requires some {{Space}}, staff, and possibly input resources consumed each month. Production Works have five sizes, each more efficient than the last. Some support Works have three sizes. Building a Work, or upgrading it by one size, takes {build_days} days.
nomad_manual.man_works_3: You can {{mothball}} a Work for free. A mothballed Work takes up Space, needs no staff, and does nothing. Mothballing or reviving a Work takes effect at the next economy tick (an economy tick happens around every three days). A mothballed support Work's effect on your fleet ends immediately.
nomad_manual.man_works_4: The Flotilla can run {support_limit_base} Fleet, Combat and Fortune Works at a time, one more at {support_limit_first} residents, and one more each time that number doubles. Economy and Capacity Works do not count. The Works that run are selected in priority order, and the rest are {{disabled}}. Disabled Works take up Space, need no staff, and do nothing. A Work reenables when the limit rises or a Work ahead of it is mothballed, scrapped or suspended.
nomad_manual.man_works_5: Some Works, and the larger sizes of others, have a {{prerequisite}}, such as a colony item installed, a character level or standing with a faction. A Work cannot be built or upgraded past a prerequisite you do not meet. If you stop meeting one, the Work is {{disabled}} at the next economy tick, and it reenables when you meet it again. A Work disabled this way does not count toward the support limit. A Work that needs a number of residents keeps running until the Flotilla is 5% under that number.
nomad_manual.man_works_6: A Work is {{idle}} while it cannot run: the Mining Rig has nothing to mine, the Foundry has nothing queued, an input is empty, or an output is full. An idle Work needs no staff.
nomad_manual.man_works_7: If you use more Space than the Flotilla has, store targets are lowered to fit at the next economy tick, and Works that still do not fit are {{suspended}}, lowest priority first. A suspended Work uses no Space and no staff, and resumes once it fits.
nomad_manual.man_priority_and_staffing_1: Residents staff your Works. Each Work has a {{priority}} of High, Medium or Low. At every economy tick, residents are assigned to High priority Works first, then Medium, then Low. A Work that does not get its staff is {{Unstaffed}} and does nothing.
nomad_manual.man_basic_needs_1: Your residents take care of their own basic needs. This is always free, but they require some Space and staffing to provide for themselves.
nomad_manual.man_basic_needs_2: All free Space and free residents are used for Basic Needs. Each level of your Flotilla's Basic Needs requires a threshold amount of both. Hover over the Basic Needs picture on the Overview tab to see these thresholds.
nomad_manual.man_basic_needs_3: A more developed Flotilla requires less. Each Work lowers the Basic Needs requirement by {{{needs_tier_relief}}} for each of its sizes, and each installed item lowers it by {{{needs_tier_relief}}}. The limit for Works and items together is {{{needs_relief_cap}}}. A mothballed, disabled or suspended Work does not count. The Military Fabricator, the Drug Lab, the Organ Harvester and the Panopticon raise it by {{{needs_tier_relief}}} for each size instead. Shops, the Theater and Luxury Quarters lower it further, past that limit.
nomad_manual.man_basic_needs_4:
There are seven levels:
    {{Non-existent}}: no Work runs, and residents leave quickly.
    {{Decrepit}}: global efficiency is {{30%}}, and residents leave.
    {{Spartan}}: global efficiency is {{70%}}. The population does not grow and no migrants join.
    {{Normal}}: global efficiency is {{100%}}, and the population grows.
    {{Nice}}, {{Lavish}} and {{Opulent}}: global efficiency is {{105%}}, {{110%}} and {{115%}}, and the population grows faster at each level.
nomad_manual.man_basic_needs_5: Support Works only have an effect while Basic Needs is {{Spartan}} or better.
nomad_manual.man_stores_1:
The Flotilla has a {{store}} for each resource commodity, and each store has a {{target}}. At every economy tick, the Flotilla tries to keep each store at its target, following the four flags next to it:
    {{In}}: If the store is under its target, automatically transfer the commodity from your cargo. Your fleet always keeps {reserve_days_supplies} days of supplies and enough fuel for {reserve_ly_fuel} light-years.
    {{Out}}: Automatically transfer anything over the target to your cargo.
    {{Sell}}: Allow the {{Brokerage}} to automatically sell anything over the target.
    {{Sell cargo}}: Allow the {{Brokerage}} to sell all of the commodity in your cargo, whatever the target.
nomad_manual.man_stores_2: The sell flags do nothing until you build a Brokerage. If {{Sell}} and {{Out}} are both on, the Brokerage sells what it can first, and the rest is transferred to your cargo. {{Out}} transfers only what your fleet has room for. If a store is still over its target after that, the Work that makes the commodity is idle until there is room.
nomad_manual.man_stores_3: A store reserves {{Space}} for its target or for its stock, whichever is larger. The minimum target is the most your Works can consume of that commodity in one economy tick. If you set a target below the current stock, the excess is sold or transferred out by the flags, and reserves Space until it is gone.
nomad_manual.man_stores_4: A new Flotilla starts with a target of {founding_store_target} for each store, and 0 for Heavy Armaments, Recreational Drugs and Harvested Organs. The stores start empty, and from the first economy tick {{In}} takes up to {founding_store_target} of each from your cargo. Every Flotilla also has {founding_space} more {{Space}} than its ships and items give.
nomad_manual.man_stores_5: {{Fill from cargo}} fills every store that has {{In}} on up to its target from your cargo, once.
nomad_manual.man_stores_6: Some factions treat Heavy Armaments, Recreational Drugs and Harvested Organs as contraband, but the {{Brokerage}} sells them like any other commodity. A patrol's cargo scan searches your cargo and not the Flotilla's stores.
nomad_manual.man_the_brokerage_1: Your Flotilla runs a financial business. The {{Brokerage}} takes a fee, giving you credits each month. It also lets you sell the commodities you marked {{Sell}} or {{Sell cargo}}, the most expensive first, at {credits_price} of base value. A larger Brokerage can sell more each month.
nomad_manual.man_mining_1: Most raw inputs come from the {{Mining Rig}}. The Flotilla mines while within range of a fully surveyed body. The speed is based on the deposit. Having multiple resource types does not decrease the individual rate. While it has nothing to mine and Remote mining is off, the Mining Rig is idle. The Mining Rig has a {{Remote mining}} toggle. With Remote mining on, the Mining Rig mines anywhere inside a star system, at a much lower rate. Remote mining takes {remote_on_days} days to turn on, and turns off immediately. While in hyperspace, or in a system with no fully surveyed deposits and no asteroids, the Mining Rig is still idle.
nomad_manual.man_the_flagship_1: The Flotilla's flagship is the ship that carries the Nomad Flagship hullmod. If the flagship is lost, sold, scuttled, mothballed or put in storage, or the hullmod is removed, the Flotilla has no flagship and is {{paused}}. A paused Flotilla produces nothing, and its residents leave over time. To resume, install the Nomad Flagship hullmod on a ship in your fleet.
nomad_manual.man_residents_1: Residents staff Works. The population grows slowly until the Berths are full. Migrants also join when you undock at an inhabited colony with Berths available, at most once every six months from each colony. You can also move crew to and from the Flotilla manually on the Overview tab.
nomad_manual.man_detaching_1: You can detach the Flotilla to hold position as its own fleet. Detached, it keeps mining and defends itself if attacked, but it consumes only from its own stores and cannot exchange cargo or crew with your fleet. Its ships consume their monthly supplies from the Flotilla's stores while detached. Bring your fleet to the detached Flotilla to rejoin.
nomad_manual.man_detaching_2: If the Flotilla's supplies store runs out while it is detached, you owe the supplies its ships consume. When the Flotilla rejoins, they are taken from your cargo, or paid for in credits if you don't have enough cargo.
nomad_manual.man_global_efficiency_1: Global efficiency is a single multiplier on how much the Flotilla produces. Below 75%, the inputs of Works scale with the outputs. From 75% to 100%, inputs are fixed but outputs continue increasing. 75% represents the floor of minimum required material to make the output, but as you become more efficient you need fewer inputs for the same output. Above 100%, a Work makes more and consumes more in the same proportion.
nomad_manual.man_global_efficiency_2:
For example, at these global efficiencies a Work makes this much output for this much input:
    {{130%}}: {{1.3}} out for {{1.3}} in
    {{125%}}: {{1.25}} out for {{1.25}} in
    {{100%}}: {{1}} out for {{1}} in
    {{75%}}: {{0.75}} out for {{1}} in
    {{50%}}: {{0.5}} out for {{0.67}} in
nomad_manual.man_global_efficiency_3: The {{Basic Needs}} level sets global efficiency. Colony items, the Guild Hall, and the Normal and Story difficulties increase it.
nomad_manual.man_global_efficiency_4: Above 100%, the {{Brokerage}}'s credits get only {brokerage_bonus_share} of the increase, and how much it can sell gets all of it. At 130% global efficiency, the Brokerage pays {brokerage_paid_at_130} of its credits and sells up to 130% as much.
nomad_manual.man_yield_1: {{Yield}} is how much a Work produces for each unit of Space. Every Work starts at a base yield, which its size and colony items can raise. Yield scales output and input together, so at double yield a Work makes twice as much and consumes twice the input. Global efficiency is separate from yield.
nomad_manual.man_the_autoforge_1: The autoforge builds ships, weapons and fighter wings in the background, one at a time. Each job needs Foundry production equal to the value of what it builds. While the queue is not empty, the {{Foundry}} Work turns stored Metals, Transplutonics, and Heavy Machinery into Foundry production, which goes to the job at the front until it is complete. Queued jobs begin once their previous job finishes. A larger Foundry produces faster, but the overall cost of the product is unchanged. Queuing a job takes no materials. The consumption begins only once something is in the queue. You manage the queue on the Foundry tab.
